Someone once asked him to prove where God is. His answer flipped the question entirely.

He's not channeling a person, a spirit, or an entity from some faraway dimension — he's going past what he calls the veil, into what he calls the static: the oneness underneath everything, which is what we all already are. So when someone challenged him, "show me where God is," his answer was simple: show me where God is not.

If everything is an extension of the same consciousness, there's nowhere left for it to be absent.

There's a version of you that never needs anyone's permission to feel okay.

Imagine total knowingness — the kind that never needs to be affirmed, validated, agreed with, or understood by anyone else. Never needing to argue your point. Never needing credit for what you did. Never needing anyone's approval to feel like you're enough. That isn't arrogance. It's a state where nothing outside you can shake what's already settled inside you.

Most people spend their whole life negotiating for a feeling they could just have.

He wears a suit, a Rolex, and drives what he wants — and he says that has nothing to do with whether he's spiritual.

Most people picture a guru barefoot in a robe, and assume money and enlightenment cancel each other out. He calls that a misnomer. The real divide was never between rich and spiritual — it's between attached and free. Love people, use things. The moment you flip that, use people, love things, that's when it costs you something real.

The biggest lie he says we've been told isn't about money. It's about where God is.

We picture God, or consciousness, or whatever word you use, as something out there — separate from us, watching from a distance. He says that's backwards. God dwells within you as you. That's the real meaning behind namaste: the divine light in me bows to that same divine light in you. No separation, ever.

And here's the part that matters most: don't believe him. Believe your own experience.

An old story, and it explains almost everything about how your life keeps repeating.

A traveler comes to a walled city and asks the guard what kind of people live there. The guard answers with a question: what kind of people did you leave behind? The traveler describes cruelty and dishonesty. "You'll find the same here," the guard says. Another traveler arrives, describes warmth and kindness in the place he came from. "You'll find the same here too."

The city never changed. He did.

There's a scientific reason an "aha moment" actually feels like something breaking loose in your body.

Old trauma sits stored as an energetic imprint — call it a samskara, or an engram, depending which tradition you ask. When a new understanding lands, the same way a note can shatter a crystal glass by matching its frequency exactly, that stored charge blows out. Not metaphorically. The frequency of the insight matches the frequency of what's been stuck, and it releases.

That's why some realizations change you instantly, and information alone never does.

Every time someone gets under your skin, you just handed them a string.

Most people go through life as a puppet — reactive, pulled by whoever pushes the right button. But once you become the observer of your own life instead of the character inside it, there's nothing left to pull. Nobody can affect you, because you've stopped being at effect and started being at cause over your own environment.

That single shift is what actually gives you the power to create.
